title: Growing Without Chasing Titles
intro: Four posts, one consistent message: do genuinely good work for people who need it, and tell it as a story.

learn.title: What compounds
learn.text:
**Do good work** — impact over visibility plays
**Work with allies** — people who already value research
**Learn on purpose** — broaden methods; certificates aren't magic
**Tell the story** — each role led to the next

On certifications: people ask about his NN/g badge constantly. His answer is that it didn't get him jobs — the work did. “Becoming a trusted, skilled partner who solves real problems” is what makes progression take care of itself.

try.q: What does Calabro say about his NN/g certification?
try.explain: Certificates aren't magic. Not the badge.

learn.title: The résumé, in two steps
learn.text:
**Step 1: Aggregate your highlights.** One bulleted list of your biggest career accomplishments — a snapshot of everything.

**Step 2: Craft targeted career narratives.** Break the career into segments and show how each role built on the last, chosen for the job you want.

A list of duties doesn't stand out in a sea of experienced candidates. A narrative does.

try.q: What is step 2 of his résumé approach?
options: Targeted narratives showing how roles built on each other
Tailoring keywords to the job advert
Cutting the résumé to one page
try.explain: Step 1 is the raw highlights list; step 2 selects and connects.

learn.title: Interviews and mentoring
learn.text:
He was laid off in 2024 and **botched two final-round case-study presentations** before changing his approach:

• Treat it as a conversation, not a rehearsed monologue
• **Show, don't narrate** every method
• Expect a mixed room — designers, PMs and leaders want decisions and impact, not statistics
• Leave out the unnecessary detail — that was the change that got him hired

**Mentoring newcomers:** skip boot camps; practise three entry-level methods — diary studies, card sorting, usability testing — guerrilla-style for a friend's or family member's business, and read the fundamental NN/g articles.

try.q: What change finally made his case-study presentations work?
options: Presenting a single project in depth
try.explain: A mixed room wants decisions and impact.

test.q: What does a mixed interview panel want to hear?
test.explain: Designers, PMs and leaders are all in the room.

test.q: Which three methods does he recommend to newcomers?
test.explain: Low barrier to entry, practised guerrilla-style. Usability testing.

test.q: What does he suggest instead of a boot camp?
options: Practising methods for a small real business
test.explain: A friend's or family member's business gives you a real context.

test.q: What is step 1 of the résumé method?
options: One list of your biggest accomplishments
test.explain: A snapshot you then select from.
Which is the context for the interview lessons.
